title: Telefónica / O2
description: Led UX, product and service design across 5 locations for Telefonica's global health and digital portfolio. Delivered a chronic disease service reducing mortality by 48%, Parkinson's voice detection at 78% precision, and pandemic prediction tools with WHO and Harvard.

metrics.label: decrease in chronic disease mortality rate

sections.title: Context
sections.body: Telefonica is one of the world's largest telecoms operators, with major consumer brands including O2 (UK), Movistar (Spain and Latin America), and Vivo (Brazil). Over five years, I led UX, product, and service design teams across 5 global locations, building a portfolio of eHealth, cloud, and data privacy products. Teams ranged from 10 to 17 people.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Telefonica was investing in health and digital services as a strategic growth area adjacent to core telecoms. The challenge was demonstrating that a telecoms company could build products with genuine clinical and commercial value — not just technology prototypes. Each product area had a distinct business problem: chronic disease management had high healthcare costs and readmission rates; Parkinson's detection had no accessible early screening pathway; epidemic tracking had weeks-long detection lag times.

sections.title: My role
sections.body: I personally led product and service design across the full portfolio. This included setting direction, leading user research programmes, designing clinical and consumer-facing interfaces, managing cross-functional teams, and maintaining relationships with clinical and institutional partners (NHS, WHO, UNICEF, Harvard). Team management and budgeting were mine; technical implementation was delegated.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Each product was grounded in field research before design began — ethnographic home visits for chronic disease, clinical workflow research for Parkinson's, mobility data analysis for pandemic prediction. I ran co-design workshops with clinical staff, facilitated cross-functional delivery, and managed the tension between the pace of a commercial product team and the rigour required by clinical and regulatory partners. Across 20+ MVPs, the selection of which 5 to launch was driven by validated demand and commercial viability, not technical interest.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body:
• 48% decrease in mortality rate for patients on the chronic disease management service
  • 63% decrease in hospital readmission rate
  • 78% precision in Parkinson's voice detection
  • 20+ MVPs developed, 5 successfully launched
  • Pandemic prediction tools validated in collaboration with WHO, UNICEF, and Harvard across Ebola and Zika outbreaks
